name: PaymentLab Fraud Investigation Tool Registry
description: Config-driven registry of tools available to the FAA-style fraud investigation agent. Each tool is categorized, sourced, and referenced to the threat report or paper that informed it.

categories.name: Transaction Context
categories.description: What happened in this specific transaction? Baseline details, amount anomalies, authentication results.
categories.question: What happened?

categories.name: Identity History
categories.description: Who is behind this transaction? Email patterns, device fingerprints, phone verification, identity graphs.
categories.question: Who is this?

categories.name: Card & Velocity
categories.description: How is this card being used? Velocity bursts, BIN lookups, card testing patterns, amount escalation.
categories.question: How is the card behaving?

categories.name: Geographic & Locale
categories.description: Do the geographic signals make sense together? Locale consistency, IP reputation, geolocation, travel feasibility.
categories.question: Where is this coming from?

categories.name: Address & Shipping
categories.description: Where is the product going? Drop addresses, AVS results, address validation, reshipping networks.
categories.question: Where is it going?

categories.name: Behavioral & Account
categories.description: Does this user's behavior match their history? Refund abuse, chargeback patterns, account age, session anomalies.
categories.question: Does the behavior make sense?

categories.name: Merchant & Product
categories.description: Is this merchant or product category high-risk? Merchant fraud rates, product type risk, historical fraud rate.
categories.question: Is this merchant/product risky?

categories.name: External Intelligence
categories.description: What do external databases say? Sanctions lists, adverse media, PEP status, breach exposure.
categories.question: What do external sources say?

tools.name: get_transaction_details
tools.description: Get full details of a specific transaction including amount, card, email, billing/shipping address, locale, and timestamps.
tools.detects: Provides baseline context — amount, card, email, billing, shipping, locale, IP, device fingerprint

references.name: FAA Framework
references.relevance: Iterative Plan→Gather→Analyze investigation loop requires transaction context as the starting point

tools.name: check_amount_anomaly
tools.description: Flag unusual transaction amounts based on customer history, merchant average, and product category norms.
tools.detects: Unusually large/small amounts, round-number fraud, amount escalation patterns (card testing → large purchase)

references.name: Luo et al. — LLM+GCN Fraud Detection
references.relevance: Most fraud is under $250; amount alone is not a signal, but anomaly relative to history is

tools.name: check_3ds_result
tools.description: Check whether 3D Secure (SCA) authentication passed, failed, was attempted, or was exempted for this transaction.
tools.detects: SCA bypass attempts, liability shift status, exemption abuse (low-value, TRA, recurring)

references.name: PSD2/PSD3 Strong Customer Authentication
references.relevance: SCA exemption abuse is a growing fraud vector in EU/EEA transactions

references.name: EPC 2025 Payment Threats Report
references.relevance: Documents SCA bypass as an emerging threat category

tools.name: get_email_history
tools.description: Get transaction history for an email address. Use to detect account patterns, multi-card usage, and synthetic identities.
tools.detects: Synthetic identities, account takeover — one email across many cards or vice versa

references.name: Luo et al. — LLM+GCN Fraud Detection
references.relevance: Email-to-card graph linkage is a key signal for fraud ring detection

tools.name: get_device_history
tools.description: Get all transactions from a specific device fingerprint. Detects device reuse across multiple accounts.
tools.detects: Device reuse across accounts, emulator/virtual machine usage, device spoofing

references.name: EBA/ECB 2025 Joint Report on Payment Fraud
references.relevance: Device fingerprinting cited as key signal for CNP fraud detection

tools.name: check_email_reputation
tools.description: Check email reputation: age, provider type (disposable vs corporate), breach history, social media presence.
tools.detects: Disposable emails (Yopmail, Guerrilla), newly created emails, emails found in breach databases

references.name: Investigation 2 — Card Testing (PaymentLab)
references.relevance: Yopmail disposable email was a key fraud signal in the card testing investigation

references.name: Unit21 AI Fraud Agents
references.relevance: Email reputation is a standard enrichment step in commercial fraud platforms

tools.name: check_phone_verification
tools.description: Verify phone number: carrier type (mobile/VOIP/landline), country, whether it matches billing address region.
tools.detects: VOIP numbers used for synthetic identities, phone-country mismatch with billing address

references.name: PCI DSS 4.0.1
references.relevance: Multi-factor authentication requirements include phone verification as an identity signal

tools.name: check_identity_graph
tools.description: Build an entity relationship graph around the transaction and detect fraud rings or synthetic identity clusters by traversing shared emails, cards, addresses, IPs, and devices.
detects: fraud rings (shared drop addresses across many cards)
synthetic identity networks (farmed accounts with linked emails/devices)
botnet / proxy clusters (many cards sharing same IP block)
device pooling (emulator farms reusing device fingerprints)

txn_id.description: The transaction ID to investigate (prefix match supported)

hops.description: Graph traversal depth: 1 = direct neighbors only, 2 = neighbors of neighbors (default). Use 2 for fraud ring detection.

references.label: Luo et al. — LLM+GCN Fraud Detection
references.note: Key insight: fraud signals emerge from relationships, not just individual features. GCN aggregates neighborhood embeddings; we approximate with BFS traversal + cluster scoring.

references.label: FAA Framework — Plan→Gather→Analyze
references.note: Graph tool fits into the Gather phase; Claude reasons over the graph structure in the Analyze phase.

references.label: EBA/ECB 2025 Joint Report
references.note: Synthetic identity fraud is fastest-growing vector; graph-based detection is recommended approach.

references.label: Investigation 1 — Shibuya Drop Address
references.note: 1-2-3 Shibuya address shared by 14 cards + 10 emails — exact pattern this tool is designed to catch.

tools.name: get_card_history
tools.description: Get all transactions for a card in the last N hours. Use to detect velocity patterns, amount escalation, and card reuse.
tools.detects: Card reuse patterns, velocity bursts, amount escalation, geographic spread

references.name: EPC 2025 Payment Threats Report
references.relevance: Card-not-present fraud with velocity patterns is the #1 payment fraud type in Europe

tools.name: check_velocity
tools.description: Check how many transactions a card made in a short window. Detects card testing and velocity bursts.
tools.detects: Card testing (rapid small transactions), brute-force BIN attacks, velocity abuse

references.name: OWASP API Security Top 10
references.relevance: Rate limiting and velocity checks are core API security controls

references.name: Investigation 2 — Card Testing (PaymentLab)
references.relevance: Amount escalation $15→$99 detected via velocity analysis

tools.name: check_bin_lookup
tools.description: Look up card BIN to get issuing bank, card type (credit/debit/prepaid), issuing country, and card brand.
tools.detects: Prepaid card fraud, issuing country mismatch with billing address, virtual card abuse

references.name: EBA/ECB 2025 Joint Report on Payment Fraud
references.relevance: BIN-level data provides more reliable card country than self-reported billing address

tools.name: check_card_testing_pattern
tools.description: Detect card testing patterns: small→large amount escalation, multiple declines followed by success, rapid sequential attempts.
tools.detects: Card testing attacks, BIN brute-forcing, stolen card validation before high-value fraud

references.name: Investigation 2 — Card Testing (PaymentLab)
references.relevance: Detected $15→$99 escalation pattern in real investigation

references.name: EPC 2025 Payment Threats Report
references.relevance: Card testing is a precursor to large-scale CNP fraud

tools.name: check_locale_consistency
tools.description: Check whether browser locale, billing country, IP country, and card country are consistent. Key signal for geo fraud.
tools.detects: Locale/country mismatches indicating proxy use, stolen cards used from different countries, geo-spoofing

references.name: PaymentLab — RAG Address Form
references.relevance: Locale signals (browser language, address format) are captured during checkout and available for consistency checks

references.name: FAA Framework
references.relevance: Geographic consistency is one of the key investigation dimensions

tools.name: get_ip_reputation
tools.description: Check IP address reputation: known proxy/VPN/Tor, datacenter IP, geographic location, historical fraud association.
tools.detects: VPN/proxy/Tor usage, datacenter IPs (bot traffic), IPs associated with previous fraud

references.name: Investigation 2 — Card Testing (PaymentLab)
references.relevance: IP geolocation mismatch (US→JP) in 11 minutes was a key fraud signal

tools.name: check_ip_geolocation
tools.description: Get precise geolocation for an IP: lat/long, city, region, ISP, connection type, proxy/VPN/Tor detection.
tools.detects: Precise location for travel feasibility checks, ISP-level anomalies, mobile vs residential vs datacenter

references.name: MaxMind GeoIP2
references.relevance: Industry standard for IP geolocation in fraud detection

tools.name: check_travel_feasibility
tools.description: Check if a human could physically travel between two transaction locations within the time gap. Uses haversine distance and realistic travel speeds.
tools.detects: Impossible travel — e.g., transactions in New York and Tokyo 11 minutes apart

references.name: Investigation 2 — Card Testing (PaymentLab)
references.relevance: US→JP in 11 minutes was physically impossible, confirming fraud

references.name: Taktile — Risk Decisioning
references.relevance: Impossible travel is a standard feature in commercial fraud decisioning platforms

tools.name: get_address_history
tools.description: Find all transactions shipped to a given address. Use to detect address reuse across cards and emails — a key drop address signal.
tools.detects: Drop addresses, reshipping fraud — multiple cards/emails shipping to same location

references.name: Investigation 1 — Drop Address (PaymentLab)
references.relevance: Shipping address used by 14 cards + 10 emails — classic drop address pattern

references.name: EBA/ECB 2025 Joint Report on Payment Fraud
references.relevance: Address reuse across accounts is a documented fraud ring indicator

tools.name: check_avs_result
tools.description: Check Address Verification Service result for this transaction: full match, partial match (zip only), or mismatch.
tools.detects: Address mismatch with card issuer records, zip-only matches (weaker signal), AVS unavailable (international cards)

references.name: PCI DSS 4.0.1
references.relevance: AVS is a required fraud prevention control for card-not-present transactions

tools.name: check_address_validation
tools.description: Validate if an address is real, deliverable, and properly formatted. Detects fake addresses, vacant lots, and PO boxes.
tools.detects: Fake addresses, vacant/condemned buildings, PO box drops, commercial vs residential classification

references.name: Investigation 2 — Card Testing (PaymentLab)
references.relevance: Fake address was a key fraud signal alongside disposable email

references.name: Google Address Validation API
references.relevance: Provides deliverability scoring and address component validation

tools.name: check_reshipping_network
tools.description: Cluster addresses receiving shipments from many different cards/emails. Detect organized reshipping operations.
tools.detects: Reshipping networks, package mule operations, organized fraud rings using shared drop points

address.description: Address to check for reshipping patterns

threshold.description: Minimum number of unique cards/emails to flag

references.name: Investigation 1 — Drop Address (PaymentLab)
references.relevance: 14 cards + 10 emails at one address = textbook reshipping pattern

references.name: EPC 2025 Payment Threats Report
references.relevance: Reshipping fraud documented as a growing organized crime vector

tools.name: get_refund_history
tools.description: Get refund history for a customer (by email or card). Detect refund abuse, return fraud, and wardrobing.
tools.detects: Refund abuse, return fraud, wardrobing (buy-use-return), excessive refund rates

references.name: EBA/ECB 2025 Joint Report on Payment Fraud
references.relevance: First-party fraud (refund/chargeback abuse) is the fastest-growing fraud category

tools.name: get_chargeback_history
tools.description: Get chargeback history for a customer or card. Detect serial chargeback abusers and friendly fraud.
tools.detects: Serial chargeback fraud, friendly fraud, chargeback-to-transaction ratio anomalies

references.name: EBA/ECB 2025 Joint Report on Payment Fraud
references.relevance: Friendly fraud / chargeback abuse is the #1 first-party fraud type

references.name: Kount — Chargeback Protection
references.relevance: Commercial platforms dedicate entire modules to chargeback pattern analysis

tools.name: check_account_age
tools.description: Check account creation date and first transaction date. New accounts with high-value transactions are high risk.
tools.detects: New account fraud, account creation bots, synthetic identity accounts created just before fraud

references.name: Unit21 AI Fraud Agents
references.relevance: Account age is a tier-1 risk signal in all commercial fraud platforms

tools.name: check_session_behavior
tools.description: Analyze user session behavior: time on site, pages visited, mouse movement patterns, form fill speed.
tools.detects: Bot behavior (instant form fill, no mouse movement), scripted attacks, account takeover (different behavior from account owner)

references.name: OWASP API Security Top 10
references.relevance: Bot detection and behavioral analysis are core API security controls

references.name: Featurespace ARIC Risk Hub
references.relevance: Adaptive behavioral analytics is the core of their real-time fraud detection

tools.name: check_merchant_risk
tools.description: Check merchant risk profile: category (MCC), historical fraud rate, average transaction value, chargeback ratio.
tools.detects: High-risk merchant categories, merchants with abnormal fraud rates, merchant compromise indicators

references.name: EPC 2025 Payment Threats Report
references.relevance: Merchant compromise and collusion are documented fraud vectors

references.name: PCI DSS 4.0.1
references.relevance: Merchant risk assessment is a requirement for payment facilitators

tools.name: check_merchant_fraud_rate
tools.description: Calculate real-time fraud rate for a merchant: fraud count / total transactions over a rolling window.
tools.detects: Merchant under attack (sudden fraud rate spike), compromised merchant, merchant collusion

references.name: Visa Merchant Monitoring Program
references.relevance: Merchants exceeding fraud rate thresholds face penalties or termination

tools.name: check_sanctions_list
tools.description: Screen customer name and address against sanctions lists (OFAC SDN, EU, UN, UK). Required for AML compliance.
tools.detects: Sanctioned individuals, sanctioned countries, sanctioned entities attempting transactions

references.name: OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List
references.relevance: US law requires sanctions screening for all financial transactions

references.name: PSD2/PSD3
references.relevance: EU AML directives require sanctions screening as part of customer due diligence

tools.name: check_adverse_media
tools.description: Screen customer against adverse media databases: fraud convictions, financial crime, money laundering, terrorism financing.
tools.detects: Known fraudsters, individuals with financial crime history, entities linked to money laundering

references.name: EBA/ECB 2025 Joint Report on Payment Fraud
references.relevance: Adverse media screening is recommended as part of enhanced due diligence

tools.name: check_pep_status
tools.description: Check if customer is a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) or related to one. Triggers enhanced due diligence.
tools.detects: PEPs requiring enhanced monitoring, family members and close associates of PEPs

references.name: FATF Recommendations
references.relevance: PEP screening is a core FATF requirement for AML compliance

tools.name: check_breach_exposure
tools.source_detail: Have I Been Pwned / SpyCloud API
tools.description: Check if customer email or credentials appear in known data breaches. Breached credentials increase account takeover risk.
tools.detects: Compromised credentials, credentials available on dark web, accounts at high risk of takeover

email.description: Email address to check against breach databases

references.name: Have I Been Pwned
references.relevance: Industry standard breach database with API access

references.name: EBA/ECB 2025 Joint Report on Payment Fraud
references.relevance: Credential stuffing from breach data is a top account takeover vector
